intro_line: Andean capital where colonial gold glitters under volcano skies.
intro: Quito rewards visitors with a UNESCO old town, mountain views and cheap, easy transport. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
transit_facts: Metro runs Quitumbe to El Labrador via Centro Histórico and La Mariscal in about 30 min; fares $0.45 general, $0.22 reduced.
Metro hours: 05:30-23:00 Mon-Fri, 07:00-23:00 Sat, 07:00-22:00 Sun and holidays.
El Trole, Metrobus and Ecovia buses cost about $0.35 per ride; pay at station entrances.
Taxis are yellow with door numbers; day minimum $1, night minimum $2, most city trips under $5.
Easy Taxi and Uber work in Quito; hotels can call a vetted taxi.
Old town is best on foot and car-free on Sundays; bikes allowed on Metro off-peak, first and last cars only.

airports.name: Nuevo Aeropuerto Internacional Mariscal Sucre
airports.note: Main gateway, about 14 km straight-line and 18 km by road east of the centre near Tababela.

options.to: Río Coca, Quitumbe or Carcelén terminals
options.note: Three routes stop outside the terminal; pay in US cash.
Look for red signs on the terminal ground floor.
Use the taxi kiosk left of the information desk; fares are listed by zone.
App pickup points may be outside the terminal; check the app.
